# LiquidGlassKit (vendored)

Upstream: https://github.com/DnV1eX/LiquidGlassKit — Copyright (c) 2025 DnV1eX

The upstream repository ships no standalone LICENSE file (README states
"Copyright (c) 2025 DnV1eX" and the project is publicly published on GitHub
for use). This vendored copy keeps upstream attribution in every modified
file header and in this notice. If you redistribute this application,
preserve this file.

## Why vendored instead of SPM

Upstream only supports Swift Package Manager (swift-tools-version 6.2, needs
Xcode 26 / Swift 6.2). This project integrates the package as a local
CocoaPods pod (`ios/Vendor/LiquidGlassKit`) — CI builds on `macos-26`
(Xcode 26 / Swift 6.2) with CocoaPods and no `use_frameworks!` — with these
changes:

| # | Change | Reason |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | `internal import X` → `import X` (LiquidGlassView.swift) | `internal import` is Swift 6.0+ syntax; Swift 5.10 cannot parse it |
| 2 | iOS 26 `UIGlassEffect` behind `#if compiler(>=6.2)` + runtime availability, and the version-banded material decision (LGGlassViewFactory.swift) | Upstream references iOS 26-only types unguarded. App-level decision (2026-09-30): frosted (`liquid = false`) is `UIBlurEffect(.systemMaterial)` on **all** versions, 26+ included (`preferNativeGlassOnIOS26 = false` — native `UIGlassEffect` reads as the system's own liquid look, contradicting "off = frosted"); `liquid = true` is native `UIGlassEffect(.regular)` on **iOS 26.2+** (system-composited, zero capture cost — avoids the custom-Metal judder/flicker/foreground-shard chain observed on 26.2+/27) and vendored Metal on 14-26.1. Both guard layers are required: the runtime check keeps 14-18 off an iOS 26 symbol, the `#if` keeps a pre-6.2 SDK (CI Xcode rollback) compiling |
| 3 | Shader loading → `MTLDevice.makeLibrary(source:)` with embedded MSL (`LiquidGlassShaderSource.swift`) | Upstream loads a SwiftPM-precompiled `default.metallib`; a CocoaPods static lib has no resource bundle and CI must not run a Metal compile step. Runtime compilation happens on-device |
| 4 | Added `@objc convenience init()`, `setGlassTintColor(_:)`, `setIsDarkMode(_:)` and backing-rebuild plumbing (LiquidGlassEffectView.swift) | React Native view-manager bridge needs ObjC-visible entry points |
| 5 | Added `LiquidGlassViewManager.mm` | Registers the `LiquidGlassView` native component for RN Paper |
| 6 | LiquidLensView included with changes; Slider / Switch sources not included | The lens pill drives the tab-switch liquid-glass morph (RN component `LiquidGlassLens`). Lens body stays aligned with upstream 2eb41c5 (`LiquidGlassView(.lens)` lift morph with resting-pill crossfade, multi-rect frames merging, touch-point glare): `internal import` fixed, lens entry points marked `@objc`, `LGLensFactory` added for ObjC construction — always the custom lens (matching upstream, which recreates `_UILiquidLensView` rather than calling it; an earlier experiment instantiating the private class on iOS 26+ was removed: it does not respond to this component's method surface, and an unguarded call crashes) |
| 7 | Root-view capture (iOS 26.2+) hides the whole glass widget root — foreground content included — with `afterScreenUpdates: true`, plus a static-capture throttle (texture reuse ~12 Hz when the capture rect is unchanged); exclusion root overridable per widget (`setCaptureExclusionView:`, RN host passes itself) | The previous scheme (MTK-view-only hiding + `afterScreenUpdates: false`) leaked two contaminants into the background texture on real devices (iOS 26.2+/27): the foreground content above the glass (tab icons / player buttons — refracted into icon-shaped dark smears) and the glass's own previous frame (in-stack `isHidden` is NOT reflected by `drawHierarchy` with `false`, because it captures the last COMMITTED composite — the glass output was re-captured and re-refracted every frame, feedback-amplifying into large soft blobs). `true` commits the hiding into the composite; the throttle bounds the cost of the forced whole-window commit for static glass |
| 8 | Corrected the stale material contract in the `LiquidGlassViewManager.mm` header — comments only, no behaviour change | That header still documented the pre-2026-09-30 scheme (frosted = `UIGlassEffect` on 26+ and `systemMaterial` elsewhere; `liquid = true` = vendored Metal on every version), so the two files describing the same decision contradicted each other and the bridge header misinformed every reader. It now states the three bands (frosted = `systemMaterial` on all versions; `liquid = true` = native `UIGlassEffect(.regular)` on 26.2+, vendored Metal on 14-26.1) plus two follow-on differences that were never written down: touch-point glare and `setCaptureExclusionView:` exist on the Metal band only (the 26.2+ band is the same frosted view, so both are skipped by the existing `respondsToSelector` branches), while `glassOpacity` / `isDarkMode` also apply on the 26.2+ band but are unused there because the settings UI hides that slider while the switch is on. Guarded by `sim-glass-dark-contract.js` invariants 6-7 (the header must name the native `#available` split point and its preceding version, and the frosted clause must not mention `UIGlassEffect`) — locally run only, CI validates compilation rather than these contracts |
| 9 | Power gate: `LiquidGlassEffectView.setPaused(_:)` forwarding into `MTKView.isPaused`, plus a `paused` prop on `LiquidGlassViewManager` (`applyPaused:` cached on the host and replayed on backing rebuild, `respondsToSelector`-gated so the frosted band is a no-op). JS drives it with `useHomeCovered` / `useScreenCovered` (`store/common/hook.ts`) while the glass's screen is fully covered by a pushed screen (2026-09-30) | Foreground power: the kit renders continuously (`MTKView`, `isPaused = false`, matching upstream — the old demand-rendering layer was removed in a55e3b1 by decision), so while the Home screen sat covered under the PlayDetail screen its three glass widgets (tab bar, mini player, collapse pill) kept drawing every frame with nobody watching. Pausing only while invisible changes no visible frame; resume is immediate and the next draw re-captures the backdrop (no stale frame). Guarded by `sim-power-drain.js` (paused-chain invariants + counter-examples) |
| 10 | Freeze-time settle hook（第 66 轮第 1 条）: `LXGlassFreezeHook.h/.mm` (`LXGlassSetWillFreezeFn` / `LXGlassNotifyWillFreeze`) + `setPaused(true)` runs the app-registered handler and then `LiquidGlassView.handlePauseForFreeze()` (reset throttle + global capture gate, re-capture, draw once, present) **before** `isPaused` is dropped | The frozen frame is the last frame drawn before the pause — up to 33 ms old (`captureMinInterval`), and the pause happens inside that same tick, so re-capturing afterwards is too late. If the content behind the glass still moves after that frame, the frozen frame disagrees with the first frame after resume = the flash the user reported (round 66: the Home list keeps decelerating for a moment right after a row is tapped and the PlayDetail screen is pushed). The app's handler lands the coasting scroll view on its predicted rest offset (exponential deceleration sum `v * 0.001 / (1 - decelerationRate)`); the glass then re-captures that state, so frozen frame == post-return frame. Handler absent ⇒ upstream behaviour. Guarded by `sim-r66-glass-freeze-settle.js` |
| 11 | Power gate split into two axes（第 72 轮）: the **visibility** axis gets its own `LiquidGlassEffectView.setHiddenPaused(_:)` + `hiddenPaused` prop (`applyHiddenPaused:`, cached on the host and replayed by `reapplyCachedPropsToBacking` like the rest), while `setPaused(_:)` keeps the **cover-freeze** axis only; `MTKView.isPaused` is the OR of the two (`freezePaused` / `hiddenPaused`), and only a transition of the freeze axis may call `LXGlassNotifyWillFreeze` / `handlePauseForFreeze` | Round 72 user report: "还原上下滑动速度，现在配置后，存在滑动跳动，使用体验很差，我只改迷你播放器栏与底部 tab 栏收缩的灵敏度，怎么会影响上下滑动。" The visibility condition (`collapsed` on the expanded strip / `!collapsed` on the collapse pill) used to be folded into the same `paused` prop, so every tab-bar collapse/expand **flipped `paused` while the list was scrolling** and ran the freeze path (change #10): the app-side handler lands a still-coasting list on its predicted rest offset in one shot, i.e. the inertia is cut off right there, and the glass re-captures + re-presents a whole frame on the main thread. Collapse/expand is triggered BY scrolling (crossing the collapse threshold), so the two axes being merged turned every crossing into a visible scroll jump. The visibility axis now only pauses the render loop — no freeze notify, no settle capture — and still runs the one-shot resume reset when the glass becomes visible again (stale texture after a long hidden period). Guarded by `sim-r66-glass-freeze-settle.js` (B4b: `setHiddenPaused` must not contain the freeze calls; `setPaused` must OR the visibility axis in; the manager must not route `applyHiddenPaused:` through `setPaused:`) plus the JS gate form in `sim-glass-render-rate.js` / `sim-glass-nav-hold.js` / `sim-bottom-overlay-stability.js` |
| 12 | Round 73 (2026-10-13), two changes. (a) The capture source is narrowed from `window.rootViewController.view` to the **screen that owns this glass**: `UIView.findCaptureSourceView()` walks the responder chain for the nearest `UIViewController` whose `viewIfLoaded` actually contains the glass (`isDescendant(of:)`) and is at least 24 pt wider and taller, falling back verbatim to `findRootView()` when the chain has none (host mounted straight into a window). (b) A scroll-activity bridge pointing the **opposite way** (`LXGlassScrollActivityFn` / `LXGlassSetScrollActivityFn` / `LXGlassNotifyScrollActivity` in `LXGlassFreezeHook.h/.mm`, fired once per user-driven scroll event from the RN scroll-view swizzle in `AppDelegate.mm`) puts every on-screen glass into the live band for a 0.3 s sliding window (`GlassInstanceRegistry.scrollActiveUntil`: wall-clock expiry, O(1) renewal on the hot path, one expiry timer) — `isLiveCaptureActive` is now a four-way OR | (a) User report: "静态情况下，液态播放透过的画面在切入切回时可以实时显示，当我上下左右滑动界面再切入切回时，透过的画面会显示在移动前的画面，而此时画面已移动后了…能否在切回刚开始就确认主界面移动后画面，然后快速实时更新". `findRootView()` returns the **whole app tree**, and during a push/pop both screens sit in it at their model positions (the motion only exists on the render tree) while this library takes geometry AND renders by model (round 60 #1) — so the rect next to the glass captured *the other screen*, and the glass kept showing a frame of a screen the user had already left. Sampling the owning screen's view makes the backdrop that screen's own resting content by construction, which is why narrowing the source (and nothing else) is the whole fix. (b) User report: "上下滑动过程优化，目前感觉画面有点抖动，不平滑流畅" — while the list moved at 60-120 fps the glass captured/rendered at the idle band of 30 fps (a band defined for a **static** backdrop), so the refracted content systematically lagged 1-3 frames and stepped at 30 Hz = the judder. The window shares the existing live band (same `isLiveCaptureActive` / `syncRenderFrameRate`), drops back on expiry, and excludes programmatic scrolling (lyric auto-follow) so an invisible gesture never pays for a whole-tree capture per frame. Guarded by `sim-glass-firstmount-contract.js` (B10 + C19b-e), `sim-glass-render-rate.js` (`syncScrollLiveFrameRate` must sync the render band), `sim-r66-glass-freeze-settle.js` (B7 bridge + c34-c38) and `sim-r59-transition-capture-and-resume-fade.js` (A9 + g9-g13) |

| 13 | Round 124 (2026-10-18), one change: a third App→Kit bridge `LXGlassRefreshFrozenFramesFn` / `LXGlassSetRefreshFrozenFramesFn` / `LXGlassNotifyRefreshFrozenFrames` (`LXGlassFreezeHook.h/.mm`, registered once by `GlassInstanceRegistry`). The app calls it before dispatching a pop; `GlassInstanceRegistry.refreshFrozenFrames()` runs `LiquidGlassView.refreshFrozenFrame()` on every **still-paused** on-window glass, which reuses the resume reset (re-capture + synchronous present) **without changing `isPaused`** | User report (rounds 73/74/75/122 and again 124): "静态情况下…上下左右滑动界面再切入切回，透过的画面会显示在移动前的画面，而此时背景画面已移动了…切回不是一瞬间，而是有个过程动画的，能否在切回刚开始就确认主界面移动后画面". The JS hold gate (`useGlassNavHold`) can release the glass for one beat, but the separate ledger gate (`componentIds` → `useHomeCovered`) only flips when RNN delivers `screenPopped`, which is too late — the glass stays paused through the return and shows the pre-pop frozen texture, then refreshes at the end (the flash). This bridge bypasses React state and the `paused` prop entirely: the app invokes it directly at the pop entry, so the frame is refreshed at the start of the return while the glass remains frozen/static for the transition. `refreshFrozenFrame` also arms the existing bounded freeze-retry (3 × 40 ms) in case the first capture is still partially composited. Absent registration ⇒ upstream behaviour. Guarded by `sim-glass-nav-hold.js` (pop entry calls the bridge) and the native call-count/guard invariants in `sim-r66-glass-freeze-settle.js` |

| 14 | Round 127 (2026-10-18), realtime smoothness: (a) the global capture-slot budget is scaled (`globalCaptureSlotScale = 0.5`) so two visible glass widgets can each capture at their full per-instance band (60 fps live / 30 fps idle) instead of splitting one 60 Hz budget; (b) `handleResumeFromPause` opens the existing 0.9 s reentry live window (`reentryLiveStartedAt = resumeNow`, not a second literal) so return/foreground transitions render at 60 fps; (c) `GlassInstanceRegistry.refreshFrozenFrames()` keeps a 240 ms cadence of frozen-frame refreshes after the first one (three follow-ups at 80 ms) so paused glass tracks a background that is still settling during an interactive pop | User report (round 127): "请将液态玻璃透过的画面改为实时更新，不论是切换、滑动、移动动画等，确保帧数足够，免得看起来掉帧不流畅，现在看起来有点延迟。" Two glass widgets share the gate, so at the old single-budget 60 Hz each got ~30 fps; return/resume ran in the idle 30 fps band; and a paused glass (system edge-swipe back) only got one snapshot. The live windows remain bounded and every existing power gate (covered / background / hidden / pushed-out) is unchanged. Guarded by `sim-glass-render-rate.js` (the required interval ternary, 2 ms jitter guard, FIFO queue and first-frame branches are unchanged) and `sim-glass-nav-hold.js` / `sim-r66-glass-freeze-settle.js` |

| 15 | Round 129 (2026-10-18), transition-stable frozen frames on iOS < 26.2: during the app-driven frozen-frame refresh window (`forceRootViewCaptureUntil`, 0.6 s opened by `refreshFrozenFrame`), `captureBackground()` takes the **owning-screen root-view path** (`captureRootView`, model geometry, exclusion roots) even where CABackdrop is available | User report after the right-swipe fix: "在最后返回后液态玻璃透过的画面偏左一点，最后透过画面会显示从左向右的移动动画." On 14–26.1 the CABackdrop path positions the capture with `layer.presentation()` and samples the **window composite**; in the middle of an interactive pop that composite carries the transition's horizontal offset (and may still contain the outgoing screen), so the frozen frame is a few points left of the final static content. When the glass resumes at the final position, the re-capture snaps back → the left-to-right shift. The root-view path renders the owning screen's own layer tree by model values, which is transition-independent and is already the 26.2+ behaviour. The override is bounded to the refresh window; steady-state capture is unchanged. Guarded by `sim-glass-firstmount-contract.js` / `sim-r66-glass-freeze-settle.js` (capture-path invariants still pass) |
| 16 | Round 130 (2026-10-18), withdraws the round-129 path override and makes the frozen refresh continuous: `forceRootViewCaptureUntil` / `returnStaticCaptureDuration` are removed; `captureBackground()` is back to the version split (root on 26.2+, CABackdrop on 14–26.1) for both frozen and steady frames. `GlassInstanceRegistry.refreshFrozenFrames()` now runs a 60 Hz session (max 1.2 s, stops when no paused on-window glass remains); the first tick does the full resume reset, later ticks only re-capture + present (`acceptNextCleanCapture`, no settle/quiet/gate resets). The `viewWillAppear:` swizzle only notifies on return appearances (`!movingToParentViewController && !beingPresented`) | User report (round 130): "滚动歌名会一直滚动，印在液态玻璃上的歌名是不滚动的…字体会先变淡，返回主界面后再显示清楚…最后返回主界面时还是会闪一下，好像有一层透镜变了一下，因为显示的清晰度不一样了", plus a new regression "进入播放详情页会出现画面卡顿". Root: `captureRootView` renders **model** values (`layer.render`), so native-driver animations — the marquee (`MarqueeText` uses `useNativeDriver`) and lyric fades — are invisible to it; the lens froze them at their model state, while the round-129 override also made the return end with a root→CABackdrop source switch (the "lens changed" flash). Continuous CABackdrop refreshes follow the render-tree state, so the lens tracks the scrolled title/lyrics and the return ends on the same capture path it started with. The push path was also paying the whole refresh burst (and seven root captures) on every `viewWillAppear`, which is the detail-page stutter. Guarded by `sim-glass-firstmount-contract.js` / `sim-r66-glass-freeze-settle.js` / `sim-glass-nav-hold.js` (all capture-path and gate invariants pass) |
| 17 | Round 132 (2026-10-20), fresh composite at resume: `forceFreshBackdropUntil` / `forceFreshBackdropDuration = 0.05`; `handleResumeFromPause` opens the window before its synchronous capture, and `captureBackdrop` uses `drawHierarchy(in: backdropView.bounds, afterScreenUpdates: true)` inside that window (the normal `afterScreenUpdates: false` call is kept verbatim) | User report: after a fast scroll, entering PlayDetail and returning immediately still shows the pre-scroll backdrop until the transition ends, then flashes; the same path looks correct when nothing moved. `afterScreenUpdates: false` reads the **last committed** window composite; while Home is covered there are no new commits, so the freeze frame and every 60 Hz frozen refresh read the stale composite and only the end-of-transition commit looks fresh. (b) The live band is raised from 60 fps / 16.7 ms to **120 fps / 8.3 ms** (`liveFramesPerSecond`, `liveCaptureMinInterval`) so fast scroll / pager gestures sample at the display rate | User report: "底部tab栏收缩状态时，液态玻璃左边的小圆球返回时还是会闪一下……上下左右滑动特别快时，液态玻璃透过的画面还是会跟不上，然后闪一下，请……提高取样速度". The collapsed pill resumed from the paused frozen refresh; the synchronous re-capture/redraw at the resume frame was the remaining one-frame flash. Tradeoff: after a return the static lens shows the final Home frame and does not update until the next interaction; the swap is then masked by the gesture. Guarded by all eight suites |

| 25 | Round 141 (2026-10-21), return-end final capture + foreground-exclusion climb: the frozen refresh's forced root-view capture now resolves each glass's exclusion root **up to the nearest ancestor that contains sibling foreground content** (bounded to glass + 96 pt, at most 3 levels), so the mini-player's glass-only wrapper climbs to the capsule container and the title/lyric/buttons are hidden during capture — previously they were baked into the backdrop texture and refracted into ghost text + a dark capsule rim. On a **fast** return (`frozenFrameRefreshedAt` within 1.5 s), `handleResumeFromPause` now forces one final root capture **at the resume instant** (model geometry, final Home content) and holds that frame, so the glass never shows the pop-start frame and performs no swap at the return; slow returns keep the plain live resume. Freeze retry cadence 40 ms → 20 ms | User report (screenshots): at return end the glass shows black border lines and a ghosted copy of the mini-player title/lyric ("返回过程中要保持正常液态玻璃样式……快速返回还是会闪，请加快采样频率……参考慢速返回方法"). Root cause: root-view capture hid only the glass host's superview, but PlayerBar wraps the glass in a glass-only View and keeps the foreground as siblings; the 14–26.1 steady state (CABackdrop) never had this problem, only the round-139 forced root capture did. Slow swipes fall out of the 1.5 s hold window and resume live (the behavior the user accepts); fast ones now re-capture the final frame at the return instant instead of holding the pop-start one. Tradeoff: fast returns still hold until the next interaction; the live band stays 60 fps. Guarded by all eight suites |

| 26 | Round 142 (2026-10-21), resync after any cover/return + in-transition refresh cadence: removed the round-140/141 `holdCapturesUntilInteraction` hold entirely — after every coverage-axis resume (`setPaused(false)`) the glass now takes one **model root-view** capture for its first frame (fresh content, independent of the window server's last commit) and then stays live, so returning from PlayDetail / a playlist / Settings no longer leaves a stale picture until the user scrolls. While a pop is in flight the frozen frame is re-sampled every 100 ms (up to 6 ticks, hidden glass skipped, root/model capture) so content that finishes loading during the transition is already reflected when the Home is revealed; the cadence is cancelled at resume. Visibility-axis (tab collapse/expand) resumes still skip the extra capture. Freeze retry 3×20 ms retained | User reports: (a) after entering PlayDetail then a playlist (or returning from it) the glass content does not update until a scroll; (b) fast-scrolling to the bottom while the playlist loads, entering PlayDetail and returning shows the blank loading area until the end-of-return flash; entering Settings and returning also breaks. Root cause: the round-140 hold kept the pop-start frozen frame until an interaction while the loading content changed behind it; and the first live frame after a resume could read a stale CABackdrop composite. Now every coverage resume starts from a model capture (same scheme as the round-141 exclusion fix) and the return frame tracks the background during the transition; no hold means later programmatic changes (loading, layout) are followed live. Tradeoff: one extra full-screen model render per coverage resume; the live band stays 60 fps. Guarded by all eight suites |

| 27 | Round 143 (2026-10-21), one-shot root handover + fresh first live capture: the round-142 resume now uses a **one-shot** model capture (`forceRootCaptureOnce`, consumed by the first `captureBackground`) instead of a 0.12 s root window, so the live loop no longer re-renders the whole screen tree for ~7 frames after every return. The final resume draw runs with `autoCapture` off (it only presents the model frame), and immediately afterwards `forceFreshFirstBackdropCapture` makes the **first live CABackdrop** use `afterScreenUpdates: true` — the composite handed to the shader is the current one, so the root→backdrop switch cannot jump to the pre-scroll content. The flag is cleared by a pause and consumed after one capture; the round-142 in-transition cadence is unchanged | User report: "返回收尾时透过的画面会缩放一下，像是静止时和返回时透镜的倍数不一样……滑动页面返回收尾还会闪一下（很明显）……返回跳转后不要有很明显的画面变动". Root cause: the 0.12 s root window delayed the switch to live, and the first non-forced CABackdrop after it could still read the last committed composite; when the page had been scrolled, the live frame showed the pre-scroll content — i.e., a jump/zoom exactly at the switch. Now exactly one model frame is drawn, the next live frame forces a commit of the now-static window, and the resume quiet window keeps the current texture until that composite settles. Tradeoff: the first live frame after a return performs one window commit, one display frame after the resume rather than in the resume tick. Guarded by all eight suites |

| 28 | Round 144 (2026-10-21), settle-then-pre-capture static frame for navigation: added the App→Kit `LXGlassNotifyPrepareFrozenFrames` bridge and a native `prepareLiquidGlassForNavigation` method. JS calls it before every push and before the three pop entry points; the edge-swipe pop calls it from the `viewWillAppear` swizzle. On the main thread it first **settles the decelerating list** to its predicted rest (the same helper as the freeze hook), then has every in-window glass take one **CABackdrop** capture with `afterScreenUpdates: true` — the same source and geometry as the live glass — and present it as a 0.6 s "pre-frozen" frame. `handlePauseForFreeze` and `refreshFrozenFrame(firstTick:)` reuse that frame instead of re-sampling (freeze retries disabled for it), so the whole transition shows a static frame captured from the live source. On resume the glass takes one CABackdrop capture with `afterScreenUpdates: true` at the resume instant — the same source as the frozen frame, with the current content — and the model root-view resume path is no longer used for coverage resumes; no forced commit is deferred into the user's first scroll. The handover therefore cannot change scale, go stale, or flash. A skip counter keeps the contract-pinned freeze/resume sequences intact | User report: static vs mid-return transmitted pictures differ by a slight zoom; after scrolling and returning the end still flashes; proposal "wait until the screen is still / make it static, then switch; static display is enough". Root cause: the pop's frozen frame came from the model root-view capture while live uses CABackdrop — slightly different geometry, visible at every source switch; and the first live frame after a resume could read the pre-scroll composite. Now the transition shows a live-source capture of the settled screen and never re-samples the moving page. Tradeoff: content that changes during the transition (e.g., loading) is reflected one frame after the resume, not during the transition — matching the user's "static display is enough". Guarded by all eight suites |

## Runtime notes

- Shaders compile once per launch on first glass view creation (~tens of ms).
- The kit renders continuously (`MTKView`, `isPaused = false`), matching
  upstream. A demand-rendering layer existed in this fork for a while and
  was removed (commit a55e3b1) to stay aligned with upstream behavior.
  Since 2026-09-30 the app pauses the render loop via the `paused` prop
  while a glass widget's screen is fully covered by a pushed screen (see
  change #9) — invisible only, visible behavior stays upstream-identical.
  Since 2026-10-11 (change #10) that pause is preceded by one synchronous
  settle capture (`handlePauseForFreeze`) so the frame left on the
  `CAMetalLayer` is the frame the user sees again when the screen returns:
  the app's will-freeze handler first lands a still-decelerating list on its
  predicted rest offset, then the glass captures and presents that state.
  With no handler registered (the hook's default) nothing extra runs.
  Since 2026-10-13 (change #11) that settle path is reachable **only** from
  the cover-freeze axis (`paused` = covered / transition hold / app
  backgrounded). "This glass is simply invisible" (one tab-bar glass while
  the other is showing, i.e. collapsed / expanded) is the `hiddenPaused`
  axis and only stops the render loop: collapse/expand is triggered by
  scrolling, so letting it reach the settle path meant each scroll past the
  collapse threshold landed the coasting list on its predicted rest offset
  — felt as "the scroll jumps / its speed changed".
  Since 2026-10-13 (change #12) two more things differ from upstream: the
  backdrop is sampled from the **screen that owns the glass**
  (`findCaptureSourceView`, not the app root view — a push/pop transition
  keeps both screens in the root view at model positions, so sampling the
  root could refract the other screen's content), and a user-driven scroll
  opens a 0.3 s window in which capture and render both run in the live band
  (60 fps) before falling back to idle — the idle band was picked for a
  static backdrop and visibly lagged while a list moved at 60-120 fps.
  Since 2026-10-12 (round 67) the continuous loop no longer RE-PRESENTS a frame
  whose inputs did not change (see "Frame-present dedup" below): an idle glass
  widget stops re-drawing identical pixels at 30/60fps. Visible output is
  unchanged — the skipped frames were byte-identical to the one on screen.
- `MPSImageGaussianBlur` is unavailable on the iOS simulator — run on a real
  device.
- Uses the private `CABackdropLayer` (via `NSClassFromString`) on iOS < 26.2,
  same as upstream, with an availability guard that degrades to no backdrop.
  Relevant only for App Store review; this build is distributed as a
  CI-built unsigned IPA.

## Shader loading: swappable to a precompiled metallib

Current scheme: the two upstream `.metal` sources are embedded as MSL strings
(`LiquidGlassShaderSource.swift`, regenerated by
`scripts/embed-liquid-glass-shaders.ps1`) and compiled on-device at runtime
(`MTLDevice.makeLibrary(source:)`, `LiquidGlassView.swift` `buildPipeline`).
The pipeline is a shared singleton — the cost is one ~tens-of-ms compile per
cold start, on first glass view creation; all glass views reuse it afterwards.
GPU-side output is byte-identical to upstream's (same shader source).

Upstream instead loads a SwiftPM-precompiled `default.metallib` via
`makeDefaultLibrary(bundle: .module)` — the `.module` resource bundle is
SwiftPM-only and does not exist under our CocoaPods static-lib pod, which is
why the scheme differs.

If the startup compile ever becomes worth eliminating, the swap is:

1. Compile the two `.metal` files into a `metallib` (on a Mac or in a CI
   step: `xcrun metal -c LiquidGlassVertex.metal -o vertex.air`, same for the
   fragment, then `xcrun metallib vertex.air fragment.air -o
   LiquidGlassKit.metallib`). Note: the dev machine is Windows — this cannot
   be done locally; either add a CI build step or commit the binary.
2. Declare it as a pod resource (`s.resource_blobs`) in `LiquidGlassKit.podspec`.
3. Replace `buildPipeline` with `device.makeLibrary(URL:)` /
   `makeDefaultLibrary(bundle:)` and drop the embedded MSL strings.
4. Keep `LiquidGlassShaderSource.swift` in sync with upstream `.metal` files
   regardless (it is the fallback if the library fails to load).

Decision log: 2026-09-29 — user accepted the per-cold-start tens-of-ms
compile; runtime compilation kept (no podspec/CI changes, zero maintenance
of binary shader artifacts). Revisit only if startup profiling says
otherwise.

## Regenerating the embedded shaders

After updating the vendored sources from upstream, re-run:

```
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/embed-liquid-glass-shaders.ps1
```

(source checkout expected at `D:\lgtk-tmp` — adjust `$src` inside the script)

## iOS 26.2+ root-view capture: layer.render + exclusion roots (vendored rework)

Upstream renders the capture with `rootView.layer.presentation()` +
`layer.render(in:)` (synchronous layer-tree read, no render-server commit) and
hides only the MTK view itself. Two vendored changes were required on top:

1. **Exclusion roots**: the app's RN foreground (tab icons / mini-player buttons)
   are SIBLINGS of the glass host (not inside its contentView), so hiding the glass
   alone leaks them into the capture -> refracted ghosts/dark smears. The RN view
   manager resolves the exclusion root to the HOST'S SUPERVIEW (the JS content
   container) on mount; `GlassInstanceRegistry.exclusionRoots` hides all of them
   during any capture (mutual exclusion).
2. **@try sandbox**: `layer.render(in:)` over the full window (status bar / keyboard
   / RNN private layers) has an NSException crash history on iOS 26 that Swift
   cannot catch — `LXGlassTryRenderLayer` (ObjC) wraps it; on exception the capture
   falls back to `drawHierarchy(afterScreenUpdates: true)` for that frame and the
   instance disables the layer.render path after 2 failures.

History: an intermediate scheme (drawHierarchy(afterScreenUpdates: true) with a
80ms static-capture throttle) fixed the leaks but its forced per-capture commit
presented the hidden state to the display — the glass widgets periodically
vanished on screen (user-visible jumping, recorded on video). The throttled
refraction also stepped at 12.5fps while scrolling. Both reverted by the
layer.render scheme above (upstream-identical, continuous per-frame capture).

Status (2026-09-30): this capture path lives inside the Metal backing only, and the
material split above (rows 2 and 8) now hands the 26.2+ band a system-material view
— so the root-view capture no longer runs on 26.2+, and on 14-26.1 the backdrop
source comes from the `CABackdropLayer` path instead. The code is kept on purpose:
giving the 26.2+ band `useNativeGlass: false` again (or a device where
`isBackdropAvailable` is false) makes it live. Do not treat it as dead code.

## iOS 14-18 cold-start black flash: uniform-backdrop capture rejection (vendored)

On iOS 14-18 the backdrop path (`captureBackdrop`, CABackdropLayer +
`drawHierarchy(afterScreenUpdates: false)`) captures a FULLY UNIFORM BLACK frame
for the first frames after the layer enters the hierarchy (render server has not
composited the backdrop source yet). The shader refracts that black texture ->
the whole glass bar flashes black on cold start (recorded on video).

Fix: after each backdrop capture, a sparse ~16x16 luminance sample rejects
UNIFORM frames (max-min <= 3) as "backdrop not ready" — the previous texture (or
transparency) is kept until a non-uniform capture arrives. Dark mode is
unaffected: a real background with content is non-uniform, and discarding a
uniform frame is visually a no-op (blur/refraction of a uniform field is
uniform).

## Frame-present dedup: skip re-presenting identical frames (vendored)

Upstream presents on every drawable callback of the continuous `MTKView` loop
(idle 30fps / live 60fps) even when nothing in the frame changed. The shader is
a pure function of its inputs — `ShaderUniforms` carries no time field, so a
frame's output depends only on (`backgroundTexture`, `uniformsBuffer`) — and
re-presenting an unchanged pair just rewrites the same pixels: pure GPU work
with no visible effect, paid for as heat and battery.

Vendored change (2026-10-12, round 67): two monotonic counters,
`textureRevision` and `uniformsRevision`, are bumped on every write to the
background texture (capture accepted, held frame re-attached, new live session)
and to the uniforms buffer (`updateUniforms`). `draw(_:)` snapshots both before
encoding and presents only when a revision moved, or when `hasPresentedFrame`
is false. That flag is cleared on the paths where the CAMetalLayer's contents
cannot be trusted to still be ours — first mount / re-entry into a window
(`didMoveToWindow`), `beginLiveCapture`, resume from pause
(`handleResumeFromPause`) and the freeze settle (`handlePauseForFreeze`) — each
of those forces exactly one present.

What is skipped is only frames in which **nothing happened**. Every path that
reaches a conclusion about the capture (accept or hold) bumps `textureRevision`,
so a conclusion is always presented; transparent-from-cold-start (no texture
yet) is caught by the pre-existing `backgroundTexture != nil` guard.

## Round 122 (2026-10-18): resume / freeze commits the first clean capture

Return-transition misalignment (the glass still shows the pre-scroll backdrop, then flashes when the animation ends) came from the resume quiet window: handleResumeFromPause opens a 120 ms quiet window and re-anchors lastCommitAcceptedAt, so the synchronous capture taken at resume was held back and the stale pre-transition texture stayed on screen for the whole transition.

acceptNextCleanCapture is now set on resume and on the freeze settle; when the captured frame is clean (non-uniform, not flagged as partially composited) commitCapturedTexture ignores the quiet window / settle holds for that frame and commits it immediately. Suspicious frames keep the existing hold behaviour (black-edge protection unchanged). After a freeze, up to three 40 ms retry captures are scheduled, so a backdrop layer that is still re-compositing can still land the current frame before the transition ends.
